transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Li (Orchid Head of ML), Marcus D'Souza (Orchid Infra), Elena Ramos (Procurement)
---
Summary (auto): Quarterly renewal/check-in to review committed retainer, add burst capacity for month-end spikes, discuss APAC + EU ramp, and contractual extension. Agreed to run benchmarks and provide pricing options (retainer + overage vs. fixed uplift). Security and network prerequisites reviewed at a high level.
---
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, first quick check—can you hear me ok?
[00:18] Jia: Yep, loud and clear, hi Alex, Samir.
[00:25] Samir (SE): Hi Jia, Marcus, Elena — excited to dig in. We put a short agenda in the invite: retainer review, burst capacity for end-of-month, regional ramp to APAC and EU, and security/handoffs.
[00:40] Marcus: Works for us. Also want to confirm timelines, we have a marketing surge scheduled late April so need APAC capacity before then if possible.
[00:55] Alex: Got it. Quick recap from last quarter: you have a reserved retainer of 120K tokens/day across dedicated pools and a small hosted fallback. Usage bumped by ~18% month-over-month, and you hit burst limits twice. Today we want to propose two options: increase retainer with a committed burst bucket, or keep the retainer and buy a predictable overage band.
[01:20] Jia: Before pricing, a technical question — our model payloads are long, avg token-length is higher, KV cache usage is heavy, so what numbers are you seeing for throughput when sequence length grows? (i'm paraphrasing)
[01:40] Samir: yeah, good point. In our bench we saw throughput drop around 1.8x for those long sequences depending on model family and quantization. We're going to run a tailored test. We'll need a couple of representative payloads from you — the one with the 4–5 KB context is the worst case.
[01:55] Jia: I'll send three payload examples, one short, one medium, one long.
[02:05] Elena: From procurement side, we need to understand how the billing will surface — is the committed retainer invoiced monthly with credits for bursts? We need a PO-friendly structure.
[02:22] Alex: Yes, we can present a PO-friendly amendment. Option A: increase committed retainer by 30% with a discount tier and define a burst pool billed monthly at N cents per 1K tokens. Option B: keep current retainer and add a burst buffer at a slightly higher rate plus auto-scale to hosted for overflow. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[02:40] Marcus: For the APAC ramp — are you proposing dedicated capacity in the closest region or a VPC/private deployment in our cloud tenancy? Latency is a big ask.
[02:55] Samir: Two approaches: 1) Dedicated pockets in our APAC region with guaranteed throughput (fastest), or 2) Redwood Private in your VPC — that gives you control and removes cross-tenant noise but requires more ops and a longer lead time. Both meet security / KMS requirements, but private gives you full KMS/HSM integration.
[03:20] Jia: What's the lead time for private? We may need something faster for the April marketing spike.
[03:28] Alex: Private typically takes 6–8 weeks for initial deployment in a new region if we need on-prem-like networking, sometimes quicker if we do a thin VPC peering pilot. Dedicated pockets we can provision in 2–3 weeks depending on capacity availability.
[03:45] Marcus: So for April, sounds like dedicated pockets in APAC is the pragmatic route and then we evaluate private for Q3.
[03:52] Samir: Agreed. We'll plan a canary for APAC dedicated first. Also note: we have automatic fallback routing so if dedicated fill up, requests can route to a lower-cost hosted variant — with explicit throttles — that's configurable in the Console.
[04:10] Jia: On security — can you confirm SOC 2 status and what audit artifacts you can share? Also SSO and RBAC mapping is important for us.
[04:25] Alex: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we'll share the SOC2 attestation and the security packet. SSO is SAML/OIDC supported and RBAC maps to groups. For data at rest we support customer-managed KMS in Private and dedicated options.
[04:45] Elena: We'll need the SOC2, pen test summary, and the data retention & deletion addendum for our legal review. A link would be helpful.
[04:55] Alex: I'll drop the security packet and the link to our security portal in the follow-up.
[05:05] [small crosstalk]
[05:20] Jia: For SLAs — our product team is asking for p95 sub-200ms for short prompts and p95 sub-600ms for long contexts. Is that realistic under dedicated in APAC?
[05:32] Samir: For short prompts on dedicated we regularly hit under 150–180ms p95 on GPU families we recommend. For long contexts p95 will vary — the way we measure is tokens/sec and KV cache hits reduce latency. We'll run the benchmarks to match your payloads and target those p95 numbers.
[05:50] Marcus: Do you have any telemetry examples? We want to see Console traces, token-level cost breakdowns and route traces so our SREs can verify.
[05:59] Samir: Yes, Console gives per-request traces, cost by token, and per-model dashboards. We'll include screenshots and a short demo recording.
[06:15] Jia: Another question — data residency in EU for a portion of traffic. We want EU-only model serving for EU customers. Can routing be policy-driven by geo?
[06:28] Alex: Absolutely, Smart routing can enforce region-bound serving. You can pin EU requests to EU-only pools and have fallback policies. We'll capture that in the design doc.
[06:40] Elena: On the financials, is there an option to do a 12-month commit for a discount vs. a month-to-month retainer?
[06:50] Alex: Yes, 12-month commit yields additional discounts and more predictable capacity. We'll present both 6- and 12-month amendment options.
[07:00] Jia: For the benchmark — can Samir run dedicated + hosted fallback scenarios so we can see failover characteristics? We want to measure tail latency under contention.
[07:10] Samir: Yep, that'll be baked into the benchmark. We'll simulate a synthetic spike and then show failover routes with metrics at p50/p95/p99.
[07:20] Marcus: Network wise we need to align on VPC peering window — we prefer maintenance windows on weekends — and firewall rules. I can send the subnet and egress restrictions.
[07:32] Alex: Great, Marcus, we'll coordinate with infra and Ops.
[07:40] [pause]
[07:55] Elena: One more procurement Q — for the burst charges, we need a hard cap or an approval workflow so we don't have uncontrolled bills. Is that possible?
[08:05] Alex: Yes, we can configure soft and hard budget caps and alerting in the Console. For hard cap you can set a quota to stop usage and for soft cap we send alerts and require approvals for overages.
[08:18] Jia: For the April spike, can we set a temporary larger soft cap with a smaller hard cap so devs can test, but stops if it goes beyond budget?
[08:27] Samir: Yes - we can do that and tag the route for the marketing campaign so it consumes from the burst pool.
[08:35] Alex: Okay, next up — contract timing. We recommend an amendment that extends the term to 12 months with the new retainer starting April 1, or a month-to-month pilot of expanded retainer for April and then convert. Which do you prefer?
[08:50] Elena: Procurement wants to see the price delta; legal would prefer a short pilot to avoid re-approvals if the numbers don't hold. They lean pilot first.
[08:58] Alex: Understood. We'll prepare a pilot quote for April—covers increased capacity with a 30-day opt-out clause, then present the 12-month amendment as a follow-up.
[09:10] Jia: For private in Q3 — any special compliance caveats? We do have PHI for small subset of EU claims so that could affect encryption and logging.
[09:22] Samir: For PHI, Private with customer-managed KMS plus audit log retention in your tenancy is the recommended path. We'll map the controls to HIPAA-like requirements — we'll include a short mapping doc.
[09:35] Marcus: About telemetry ingestion and retention — can we hold logs for 90 days and export them to our Splunk?
[09:43] Alex: Yes, logs can be retained per your retention policy and exported to Splunk via our export connectors. We'll capture retention settings in the SOW.
[09:54] [background noise briefly]
[10:05] Alex: I'll summarize what we need from you to run the bench: sample payloads, peak-hour profile, SLA targets, and a list of endpoints that need EU-only routing.
[10:15] Jia: I'll get that to you tomorrow.
[10:20] Samir: Great. On the benchmark side we'll test three configurations: (A) Dedicated pockets in APAC (B) Dedicated pockets + hosted fallback (C) Private trial (if you want but that will be longer). We'll publish a short runbook for the tests.
[10:35] Elena: Also, please include a line item for professional services for the initial peering and onboarding — we need that for the PO.
[10:44] Alex: We'll include PS estimates and a per-region provisioning fee.
[10:50] Jia: Any known blockers you anticipate for the April pilot?
[10:55] Samir: Only capacity lead times — we'll flag if we can't provision the dedicated pocket quickly enough; otherwise network peering is the other potential delay but Marcus is taking that.
[11:05] Marcus: I'll coordinate the peering docs this week.
[11:10] Alex: Sound good. Anything else on pricing?
[11:15] Elena: Please ensure the pricing spreadsheet shows monthly committed token allowances, burst buffer pricing, and a sample month cost at projected traffic. 
[11:24] Alex: Will do. We'll also show model selection tips to reduce cost — quantization recommendations and batching suggestions from Optimize.
[11:34] Jia: Quick piece of feedback — your console screenshots previously looked great; if you can include a small video walkthrough that would help SRE and product.
[11:42] Samir: We'll record a 10-minute walkthrough and attach it.
[11:46] Alex: Alright let's recap and agree next steps.
[11:50] Recap: 1) Alex sends pricing + security packet + PS estimate by 2027-03-12. 2) Jia sends payloads and SLAs by 2027-03-11. 3) Samir runs benchmarks and shares results by 2027-03-16. 4) Marcus shares peering config by 2027-03-14. 5) Elena provides procurement window by 2027-03-18.
[12:20] Jia: That sounds right. Thanks everyone.
[12:30] Elena: Thanks, bye.
[12:33] Alex: Thanks all, we will follow up with the links and sheet.
[12:40] [call ends]

Notes/Artifacts referenced: pricing_spreadsheet_v2.xlsx (link), redwood-security-packet.pdf (link), console-demo-recording.mp4 (link), bench-runbook.md (link)
